own_scenes.family: Raíces: funk, disco, Jamaica y las calles del Bronx
own_scenes.desc: Mientras el Bronx bailaba breaks, en la escena disco para mayores DJ Hollywood, heredero de Jocko Henderson, Pigmeat Markham, Gil Scott-Heron y Rudy Ray Moore, introdujo el rap rítmico con llamada y respuesta: voz de oro, cartel en el Apollo, quinientos dólares por noche en cuatro o cinco clubes. Eddie Cheeba fue el primero al que Russell Simmons vio rapear en directo, con Easy G a los platos («On, and on… like hot butter on what?» «Popcorn»); Lovebug Starski, DJ residente del Disco Fever, unió los dos estilos. Para Kool Moe Dee el hip hop moderno es la fusión de las dos corrientes: el lado Hollywood, con llamada y respuesta sobre disco, y el lado Herc, de breakbeats para b-boys. Las «shoe people» (adultos de traje) y las «sneaker people» (los chavales de deportivas).

influences.name: Los sound systems: Grandmaster Flowers, Pete DJ Jones y Disco King Mario

refs.q: There are two different strands of hip-hop: the Hollywood side with the call-and-response, over disco records; and the Herc side is a similar thing, but is old breakbeats and b-boy records.
refs.para: Kool Moe Dee (artist, Treacherous Three): There are two different strands of hip-hop: the Hollywood side with the call-and-response, over disco records; and the Herc side is a similar thing, but is old breakbeats and b-boy records. The merging of those two is what really forms what we’re calling today’s modern hip-hop. Which if you trace further back, you can go until the gospel quartets and see that those styles were around way before we were there, because that’s where you got Pigmeat Markham and Jocko [Henderson] and all the guys that were doing it at a time when it just never caught fire and never created the landscape that we did, where everybody that was a teenager at that time, and I’m talking mid to late ’70s, everybody was caught up in what we now call hip-hop.

refs.q: His poetry, his showmanship, it was like nothing I’d seen before. And the crowd participation. It was magical.
refs.para: He wasn’t DJing and rapping. He had Easy G cutting and he wasn’t echo-chambering his name. His poetry, his showmanship, it was like nothing I’d seen before. And the crowd participation. It was magical.
